clue.text: Every real Puritan regularly offered praise to God

parts.note: every can mean all, as in 'all the time'

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words real and Puritan

explanation.surface: Every genuine Puritan dutifully gave thanks to the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and later even letters of 'real' and 'Puritan'; 'offered' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew-derived liturgical cry is a shout of worship meaning 'praise the Lord'.

clue.text: Computer device reduced by 50% for a limited period

indicators.note: reduced by 50% says the word loses its second half, four of its eight letters

parts.note: a terminal is a screen and keyboard connected to a computer

explanation.surface: A gadget gets cut down in size for a short while only.
explanation.definitionFit: A school term or a term of office is a fixed span of time.

clue.text: Lean, lissome, agreeable nurse

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so these words hold the answer inside them across the comma

explanation.surface: A list of virtues for a slim, pleasant nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like the subject being described; it is the verb holding the letters in lissoME AGREeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean in the sense of scanty or thin, as in lean years, is a synonym.

clue.text: Scots community refuses to consume cake

indicators.note: refuses here means turns away, so a word is rejected and dropped from the town's name

parts.note: Bannockburn is a town near Stirling in Scotland, site of a famous 1314 battle
to burn is to consume, as fire consumes fuel

explanation.surface: Some Scottish village won't eat a certain dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNOCKBURN is a Scottish town; take away BURN and what is left is the Scottish flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bannock is a round flat Scottish oatcake or griddle cake.

clue.text: Strategy to introduce piano into Asian orchestra

indicators.note: to introduce one thing into another is to put it inside, so the musical letter goes within the ensemble's name

parts.note: a gamelan is a traditional Indonesian ensemble of gongs and metallophones
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A plan to bring a piano into an Indonesian percussion ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce ... into' signals the container; P goes between the E and the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is an overall scheme of action, a strategy in sport or business.

clue.text: It's not terribly clever to box, we've found

indicators.note: to box is to enclose in a box, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd, as in a cute move

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that being a boxer is not a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clever' as cute is an older sense meaning sharp or shrewd; 'terribly' scrambles the apostrophe-free letters of the first two words, and 'to box' wraps the adjective round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an organisation is to establish or set it up, which is one sense of constitute.

clue.text: Make good move

definitions.meaning: to make good something damaged is to mend or fix it
to go somewhere, as in withdrawing to the drawing room

explanation.definitionFit: Repair means mend; repair to a place means go or move there, a formal idiom.

clue.text: A person who likes sandwiches finally chose one that's succulent!

indicators.note: sandwiches means placing something between two slices, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a lover is someone who likes something, as in a music lover

indicators.note: finally points at the end letter of the word chose

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Someone fond of sandwiches eventually picks a juicy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food; it is the verb putting E (the end of 'chose') inside LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a fleshy-leaved plant, a classic succulent.

clue.text: American writer describing Georgia's highest point

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, as in describing a circle, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales of horror
GE is the international country code for Georgia

explanation.surface: An American author writing about the summit of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense: Poe 'describes' (draws round) GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the farthest point of an orbit, hence figuratively a peak or climax.

clue.text: Molotov once rejected elements of Communism, reportedly

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
elements of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Soviet minister turns away from parts of communist doctrine, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Molotov looks like the Soviet politician; it is the city in the Urals named after him from 1940 to 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city of Perm bore the name Molotov for seventeen years in the Soviet era.

clue.text: Joe and Geri pretty much take the biscuit!

parts.note: GI Joe is a nickname for an American soldier, a GI
'n' is a casual short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll

indicators.note: pretty much means nearly all of the name, so its final letter goes

parts.note: to snap is to take a photograph

explanation.surface: Two celebrities, one of them Geri Halliwell, behave outrageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous; Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp ginger-flavoured biscuit, i.e. a cookie.

clue.text: Augmentation of bottom and breasts left me without a supply of money

parts.note: a bust is a woman's bosom

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed from the word me

parts.note: M is the economists' symbol for money supply, as in M1 or M3

explanation.surface: Someone after cosmetic surgery to the bust and behind finds themselves broke.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST + L + E, where E is ME after losing M, the money-supply symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle was a pad or frame worn under a skirt to fill out the rear.

clue.text: Be in no hurry to eat one's meals with Yankee

parts.note: to take food is to eat it
one gives I, the Roman numeral, with 's as 'is'
teas are light afternoon or evening meals in Britain
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Advice to dine slowly, alongside an American.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can mean an evening meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To take things easy is an idiom for relaxing and not rushing.

clue.text: Keen to protect boy in workplace

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
Ollie is a boy's name, short for Oliver

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic worker looks after a lad on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb meaning wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine, a place where miners work.

clue.text: President who is snide about English-speaking nation

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic or snide
Oz is an informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A leader with a sneering attitude towards an anglophone country.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy was President of France when this puzzle appeared in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Sarkozy served as President of the French Republic, 2007 to 2012.

clue.text: Country in recession? Business accepts course we must follow

indicators.note: must follow means the next piece comes after the others
accepts means takes in, so one piece holds another
in recession means going back, so the word is reversed in this down clue

parts.note: biz is informal for business, as in show biz
an MBA is a postgraduate business course
taken as written

explanation.surface: An economy shrinking while a firm takes on a training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reverses the short form of business, and 'accepts' puts the degree course inside; the surface nods to the country's economic collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa.

clue.text: Hapless, gutless president is ousted

indicators.note: is ousted means removed from office, so the letter for the leader is thrown out

parts.note: lacking guts, i.e. not plucky

explanation.surface: A spineless head of state who is unfortunate is thrown out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' gives UNPLUCKY, an invented negative of plucky; removing P leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hapless has no luck, which is the plain meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Fantastic innings at an end

parts.note: in cricket a batsman's innings is often called a knock
out means finished, as in before the day is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting turn has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a batsman's turn at the crease in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is something stunning; as an adjective it means excellent or sensational.

clue.text: Done any running? It's rather dull

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about having gone jogging, judged boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, so lacking interest.

clue.text: A charming, endlessly dynamic president

indicators.note: dynamic means energetic and shifting, so the letters move around
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A description of a charismatic, energetic leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CHARMING to CHARMIN, and 'dynamic' rearranges A CHARMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The president of a company or committee is its chair, who presides.

clue.text: Noble gas — argon — is periodically cloudy

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

indicators.note: periodically means at intervals, taking every other letter of the words argon and is

parts.note: c stands for cloudy in weather notation

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a noble gas, argon, sometimes looks murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble gas' reads as one chemical term, but 'Noble' is the definition; 'periodically' plays on the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic conduct is brave and high-minded, as noble deeds are.

clue.text: Measure of acidity has turned isolated compound

parts.note: pH is the scale measuring acidity

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: lone means solitary or isolated

explanation.surface: An acidity reading has changed after a substance was separated out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses LONE to ENOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, or carbolic acid, is an organic chemical compound.

clue.text: Once retired, a chap put on old man's hat

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: once retired means after being sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A pensioner wearing his father's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once retired' turns the article and chap backwards; 'old man' is British slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat.

clue.text: Being generous in giving mean Mafioso unconditional forgiveness

parts.note: free with something means giving it generously
par is a norm or average, a mean
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: A gangster shows kindness in granting complete absolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like 'stingy', contrasting with 'generous'; it is the average.
explanation.definitionFit: A free pardon is a full legal pardon cancelling a conviction.

clue.text: Doctor cut hand shaving

indicators.note: cut means removed, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a shaving is a thin flake, as of wood
L is the left hand, as in L and R for left and right

explanation.surface: A medic nicked his hand while shaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the verb meaning falsify; 'shaving' is a noun giving FLAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to tamper with them, to falsify.

clue.text: Knox, perhaps, struggled to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: fought means struggled or battled

explanation.surface: A man named Knox, possibly, fought to make himself audible.
explanation.walkthrough: Fort Knox is the US Army post holding gold reserves; in non-rhotic speech 'fought' and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Knox is a fort, so the name gives an example of the answer.

clue.text: Bob grasped sharp tool

parts.note: to bob is to move up and down, to jig
saw means understood, as in 'I saw what he meant'

explanation.surface: A man named Bob gripped a cutting implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a power saw with a fine blade for cutting curves.

clue.text: Our men going off to join American legion

indicators.note: going off means exploding or departing, so the letters scatter

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers leave to enlist in a US regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legion' looks like a noun; it is the adjective meaning many, as in 'their number is legion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means very many, a literary synonym.
